sections.title: MARGIN LADDER
sections.note: 'OPM' in Indian screeners is the EBITDA margin; the EBIT margin is a different number. Both are labelled explicitly here so they are never mixed.

sections.title: RETURNS ON CAPITAL
sections.note: Return on capital, not margin, is what compounds. Invested capital is computed by both routes and reconciled; a material gap means something is misclassified. ROIC excluding goodwill measures the operations, ROIC including it measures capital allocation - both are shown.

sections.title: DUPONT - 3 STEP  (ROE = net margin x asset turnover x equity multiplier)
sections.note: Answers 'what kind of business is this'. Average balances are used, so the product reconciles exactly to ROE.

sections.title: DUPONT - 5 STEP  (ROE = tax burden x interest burden x EBIT margin x asset turnover x leverage)
sections.note: Separates operations-driven ROE (margin x turnover) from financing-driven ROE (tax burden, interest burden, leverage). Two firms with the same ROE and different decompositions are not comparable investments. Note that the interest burden can exceed 1.0 where other income is large, since PBT then sits above EBIT.

scalars.name: ROE driver over the full period

sections.title: INCREMENTAL RETURNS
sections.note: Average ROIC is history; ROIIC is the forecast. The capital denominator is lagged one year because capital takes time to earn. Blended ROIC drifts toward ROIIC as new capital dominates the base - which is why a company can report record profits for years while every new rupee destroys value.

scalars.name: ROIIC basis
scalars.value: 3-year, capital lagged one year (FY2022..FY2025 vs capital FY2021..FY2024)

sections.title: LEVERAGE AND COVERAGE
sections.note: Debt includes capitalised lease liabilities throughout. Net debt deducts cash and current investments (Indian filings park surplus treasury in current investments, not in cash). Every band is sector-dependent: 3x net debt/EBITDA is prudent for a contracted utility and reckless for a mid-cap with a 200-day cash cycle.

sections.title: WORKING CAPITAL
sections.note: Days are computed on average balances. A CCC that improves because DPO jumped is supplier financing, and a CCC that improves because receivables were factored is a balance-sheet transaction - neither is an operating gain, and both reverse.

metrics.name: Change in NWC / change in revenue

sections.title: CASH FLOW QUALITY
sections.note: The Sloan accrual ratio -- (net income - CFO) / average total assets -- is one of the most robust anomalies in the literature: above roughly 10% is a red flag for earnings reversal.

sections.title: PER SHARE
sections.note: Computed on the diluted count where supplied (basic count otherwise). A count lifted from the cover of a filing understates the claim on the business wherever options, RSUs, warrants, CCPS or convertibles exist.

sections.title: VALUATION (on FY2025)
sections.note: Multiples are computed on the latest supplied period only. A multiple without an as-of date and a stated earnings basis is not usable.

quality_warnings.detail: Receivables compounded at 10.9% against revenue at 3.3% over FY2021-FY2025, a gap of 7.6 percentage points. That is the classic signature of pulled-forward revenue, channel stuffing or weakening customers. Read the Schedule III receivables ageing schedule and check the over-6-month bucket before accepting the headline DSO.

Receivable days moved from 25 (FY2022) to 32 (FY2025), +27.3%, rising in every single year. Rising DSO is the earliest sign of channel stuffing, weakening customers or aggressive revenue recognition; distinguish it from a deliberate credit-terms change and check whether any apparent improvement came from factoring.

Tax tests flagged: a swing of 10.8 percentage points across the period. A tax rate that moves without a regime change usually signals one-off credits, MAT credit utilisation, an expiring tax holiday about to reverse, or aggressive positions under dispute - each of which makes the current post-tax earnings a poor guide to the next year's.

method_notes: NOPAT uses a normalised tax rate of 16.9% (aggregate tax charge / aggregate PBT over FY2021, FY2022, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025), not any single year's effective rate. India: an entity that elected s.115BAA is not comparable to its own pre-FY20 history - hold the rate constant for cross-cycle work.
Balance-sheet denominators use the average of opening and closing balances wherever a prior period exists; the earliest period necessarily uses closing balances.
Periods are assumed to be 1.00 year(s) apart (change with --period-years).
